--- title: "sjPlot: Visualizing Regression Models in R" --- ## Introduction ### Overview The `sjPlot` package provides tools for creating publication-ready visualizations and tables for statistical models, survey data, and cross-tabulations. Key functions include: - `sjPlot::plot_model()`: Visualizes regression model effects - `sjPlot::tab_model()`: Creates HTML/Markdown tables for model summaries - `sjPlot::tab_xtab()`: Generates contingency tables with statistics ### Use Cases - Visualizing interactions in mixed-effects models - Reporting odds ratios from logistic regression - Creating APA-style frequency tables ### Benefits - Unified syntax for diverse model types (lm, glm, lme4) - Automatic effect size calculations - Seamless integration with `ggplot2` for customization ## Getting Started ### Loading the Package ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pacman::p_load(sjPlot, lme4, ggplot2, ggpubr, effects) theme_set(theme_pubr()) ``` ::: ### Basic Usage ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Fit a linear model model <- lm(mpg ~ wt + cyl + gear, data = mtcars) # Create effect plot plot_model(model, type = "eff", terms = "wt") |> ggplot2::ggtitle("Effect of Weight on MPG") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` $title ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](sjPlot_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` $subtitle [1] "Effect of Weight on MPG" attr(,"class") [1] "labels" ``` ::: ::: ## Key Functions and Features ### plot_model() **Description:** Visualizes regression coefficients or marginal effects **Syntax:** ```r sjPlot::plot_model( model, type = c("est", "eff", "pred"), terms = NULL, show.values = TRUE ) ``` **Example:** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Fit mixed-effects model mixed_model <- lme4::lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject), data = sleepstudy) # Plot coefficients plot_model(mixed_model, type = "est", title = "Sleep Study Coefficients") + ggplot2::theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](sjPlot_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ### tab_model() **Description:** Creates formatted model summary tables **Syntax:** ```r sjPlot::tab_model( ..., show.ci = TRUE, show.aic = TRUE, string.pred = "Predictor" ) ``` **Example:** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} glm_model <- glm(vs ~ wt + mpg, data = mtcars, family = binomial) tab_model( glm_model, show.r2 = TRUE, pred.labels = c("Intercept", "Weight", "MPG") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

````` ::: ::: ## In-Depth Examples ### Example 1: Prediction plot for Interaction Effects Visualization **Objective:** Demonstrate temperature × insulation interaction in housing data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data(housing, package = "MASS") model_interaction <- glm( Freq ~ Type * Cont + Sat + Infl, family = poisson, data = housing ) anova(model_interaction) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
| | Df| Deviance| Resid. Df| Resid. Dev| Pr(>Chi)| |:---------|--:|---------:|---------:|----------:|--------:| |NULL | NA| NA| 71| 833.6570| NA| |Type | 3| 376.30001| 68| 457.3570| 0| |Cont | 1| 38.83207| 67| 418.5249| 0| |Sat | 2| 44.65689| 65| 373.8680| 0| |Infl | 2| 78.51627| 63| 295.3518| 0| |Type:Cont | 3| 39.05780| 60| 256.2940| 0|
::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_model( model_interaction, type = "pred", terms = c("Type", "Cont"), axis.title = "Type of rental accommodation" ) + ggplot2::scale_color_viridis_d() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Prediction Plot of Interaction Effects](sjPlot_files/figure-html/fig-interaction-plot-1.png){#fig-interaction-plot width=672} ::: ::: ## Advanced Features ### Customization Modify table appearances using built-in themes: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tab_model( glm_model, CSS = list(css.table = "color: blue;"), title = "Customized Model Table" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

````` ::: ::: ### Integration with Ggplot2 ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_model(mixed_model, type = "re") + ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(labels = c("Subject 1", "Subject 2")) + ggplot2::labs(caption = "Random Effects Plot") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](sjPlot_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Troubleshooting and FAQs ### Common Issues **Problem:** "Model class not supported" error **Solution:** Convert models using `sjPlot::convert_to_sjmodel()` **Problem:** Missing confidence intervals **Solution:** Specify `ci.lvl` in plot_model: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_model(model, ci.lvl = 0.99) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](sjPlot_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ### FAQs **Q:** How to export tables to Word? **A:** Use `flextable::save_as_docx()`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tab_model(model) |> flextable::save_as_docx(path = "table.docx") ``` ::: ## Best Practices 1. Use model wrappers for complex objects: ```r sjPlot::tab_model(lme4::lmer(...)) ``` 2. Maintain consistent theming: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sjPlot::set_theme( theme = "539", axis.title.size = .9, geom.label.size = 3 ) ``` ::: ## Conclusion ### Summary - `sjPlot` streamlines statistical reporting through unified visualization syntax - Key functions support >30 model types from common R packages ### Next Steps - Explore `plot_stackfrq()` for Likert scale visualization - Experiment with `tab_mixed()` for mixed-model comparisons ## References and Resources - [Official Documentation](https://strengejacke.github.io/sjPlot/) - [CRAN Vignettes](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=sjPlot) - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/strengejacke/sjPlot/issues)
